DataPipe saves **one CSV file per participant**. This document reads all of
them and finds the average typicality rating for each animal.

## Load packages

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

## Read in all the data files

The files in `data/example/` are practice runs with random slider positions.
For your real data, download the files from your Google Drive into
`data/raw/` and change `"example"` to `"raw"` below.

```{r}
files <- list.files(here("data", "example"), full.names = TRUE)
files
```

`read_csv()` can read a whole list of files and stack them into one table.

```{r}
all_data <- read_csv(files, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Keep only the rating trials

The `response` column also holds the keys people pressed on the welcome
screens (like `"a"`), so R reads it as text. Once we keep only the rating
trials, we turn it back into numbers with `as.numeric()`.

```{r}
ratings <- all_data |>
  filter(task == "rating") |>
  mutate(response = as.numeric(response)) |>
  select(animal, response)

ratings
```

## Average rating for each animal

```{r}
animal_means <- ratings |>
  group_by(animal) |>
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(response))

animal_means
```

```{r}
ggplot(animal_means, aes(x = mean_rating, y = animal)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Mean typicality rating (0-100)", y = "Animal")
```
